instruction: Create a basic systemd service unit that runs a script
output:
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/myapp.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=My Custom App
After=network.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/myapp
Restart=on-failure
User=myapp

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

Create a simple forking service unit
output:
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/mydaemon.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=My Forking Daemon

[Service]
Type=forking
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/mydaemon
PIDFile=/run/mydaemon.pid

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

instruction: Create a oneshot service that runs once at boot
output:
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/init-setup.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=One-time setup

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/setup.sh
RemainAfterExit=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

Set CPU and memory limits on a service
output:
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/limited.service <<'EOF'
[Service]
CPUQuota=50%
MemoryMax=256M
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/heavy-app
EOF

instruction: Configure a service to restart always with delay
output:
sudo systemctl edit --dropin=restartlimit myapp <<'EOF'
[Service]
Restart=always
RestartSec=30
StartLimitIntervalSec=300
EOF
